chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Mosby's Dixieland Blue Blowers at Solomon's Dance Pavilion
summary: Solomon's on Grand Avenue held thousands daily; Henry Starr led the piano there after his first cabaret job with Spikes.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Let's see. Mosby's Dixieland Blue Blowers in 1925 were then in their seventh month at Solomon's Dance Pavilion...
Solomon's Dance Pavilion De Luxe! Grand Avenue and what? About where on Grand?

Oh, I think it was Grand Avenue and Twelfth--or something like that. Or Grand Avenue and Ninth, I think it was. Ninth and Tenth. That was a big dancehall there, you know, and they played there afternoon and night. They had two sessions a day, and that was a...they had just thousands of people there every day. You know. Solomon's.
And it says they had Harry Barken on trumpet; Lloyd Allen, trombone; H.L. Brassfield, saxophone; Henry Starr, piano and leader, and...
I told you I...when Jelly Roll left me up there that night that I had to go out and get Henry. That was his first job in a cabaret.
Did Jelly Roll catch up with Anita that night?
